I could just hear the people talking on the phone. I do not know how, but when I pick up the phone and before I start dialling the numbers, I hear someone on the phone talking already. I do not know somehow but I get the conversation between two people, you know, and toward them, you know, one man was saying, you know, "What are you doing? I mean, you are shelling them but you are also shelling us". The other man told him, "Do not worry, everything is under control. We are going to, you know, do this fast and very quick. Everything is going to be OK". Then I tried again to contact someone but I could not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps it would be useful if we asked for Exhibit 79 and have the witness point out exactly where his village is? 79.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Where his village is?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, that would be helpful. Tell us how far. I gather it is very, very, very close to Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I think the witness indicated six kilometres but I will ask him again.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Six kilometres? Good.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sir, if you could take a moment and orient yourself with that map and then we will -----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If that could be placed on the overhead projector and perhaps you could indicate with the pointer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated).

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That is the village of Kevljani?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could move back a bit, perhaps could you also indicate where Kozarac is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated).

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Just for general orientation purposes, does this map show us where Prijedor is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Could you point that out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated].

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. After the initial chaos and panic, was a decision made by the people in the village about what to do or where to go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was decided?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We decided to go in nearby river and hide.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did most of the villagers do so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, most of them, the majority of people did but some people left in the village -- stayed in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did the people stay give any reasons for staying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know only for three people, myself, who stayed, maybe more stayed, but for one of them, it was my relative and my first neighbour was World War II veteran, and he just told us, you know, he is not going. He wants, if something happen, he wants to die in front of his house because he has already been through that once, and for him going somewhere to hide, it does not make any difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You say the villagers decided to go to the river. How high was the river at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean the water?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not much water. In fact, it was a very small river and, you know, when it is spring or summer sometimes almost there is none of it, but just a little, not much.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Had there been some talk about the possibility of going to the nearby woods?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was that one of the logical possibilities for shelter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It was, but someone figured out that the river was a better place to hide than those woods, and in the end it really was a better place than those woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How long did the shelling last after you and the other villagers fled to the river?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All day and all night, but not constantly. You know, they would shell us for 15 and 20 minutes and then they will stop, and then will, you know, they start firing bullets from all different kind of calibres, calibres of weapons. You know, you see through the air those trace of bullets. You could see them, you know, going through the leaves or the trees. Then they will stop shelling and again start shelling and on and on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You had mentioned that the possibility of going to the forest for shelter was considered but rejected. In the morning, were you able to see what would have happened to the villagers if they had, in fact, sought shelter in the woods?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, most of us would be killed if we were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Why was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because most of the shells fell in that forest.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was there any reason, as far as you know, to shell the forest other than the possibility that the villagers might be there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That next morning, did you and the other villagers of Kevljani receive information about what to do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we did. One of my friends, he had a small radio, and he heard on the radio station from Prijedor that we are supposed to surrender by 10 o'clock or they are going to come to the village and, you know, destroy everything and kill everyone in sight.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did the villagers then decide to surrender?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How did you and the others indicate that you were surrendering?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, first some put their white flag on the mosque, and then two men which I know, they also took a white flag and from the place where we were, they were going to the school where the Serbian Army or whoever was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did these people who went to meet with representatives of the Serb army return to where the villagers were and tell you what the villagers were supposed to do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did. They returned and told us that we are supposed to go, all of us, to that place, where it was that primary school, and they are going to meet us there, I mean, they are going to wait up there for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you and the other villagers arrived at the school, the area of the school in the village, what did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we arrived at that area, I mean, the school, it was partially destroyed by shell, you know, from tank grenade, they are firing that. The house on the right side was also destroyed, and around us, around that area, was Serbian soldiers and the road we were going to that school was also, you know, surrounded by the Serbian soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What were the Serbian soldiers wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some of them were wearing those regular SMB uniforms. Some of them were wearing those camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of the Serbian soldiers who were there, either by name or by face?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I recognised two because I know them before, they were going with me in school, and around 10 or 12 of them I recognised just by their face, I had seen before.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were there some soldiers whom you did not recognise?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were. When we were taken to the field and we sat down, you know, they were going through where we were sitting, you know, and we could hear them talking and some of them were talking with a Serbian dialect which was really unusual for -- and I did not know and I never saw him before that, and with that dialect which is fairly unusual in that area, because even Serbs they are talking the same way I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you recognise the leader of this group of Serbian soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who was that and where was he from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not know his full name. I just know him by his nickname Cigo and he is either from Omarska or surrounding village around Omarska. I do not know really.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did the villagers of Kevljani surrender any weapons as they went to the school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As far as you know, did every villager who had a weapon surrender it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: About how many weapons were collected and what kind of weapons were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was maybe around 40 weapons, a few of them, those automatic guns, a few of them also semi-automatic, long, you know, yes, semi-automatic, and most of the weapons were some kind of home-made, I mean, the villagers made themselves which was very dangerous even to use because you never know if you fired that if you are going to blow up your hand or it is really going to work.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were the Serb forces looking for particular people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How did they go about calling for particular people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, Cigo, he came in front of all of us, and he had a list in front of him and he was reading the names. For most of those people at that time, they worked in Croatia. You know, they were working there. So, around nine or 10 of them were there at that time and they took them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where did they take them and could you tell what happened to them after they were taken there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They took them inside the school, and when they got in you could just hear screaming and yelling died away. So, I do not know if they scream for fun or they were beaten.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was it your impression, based on what you were hearing at the time, that these people were being beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was the Serbian media present?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What were they doing? Were they filming?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were filming us sitting there in that field and, you know, they were just saying another religious liberator from Muslim extremists.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So far as you knew, were there were any Muslim extremists in your village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were some of the villagers of Kevljani taken by Serbian forces to the houses of the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were. They told us, Cigo told us because he was in charge so he was saying everything what to do, they are going to take some of the people with their patrol and they are going to go inside the village and check out the house and everything, are there any more weapons or anyone else in there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After that process was completed what did Cigo tell the villagers of Kevljani?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He told us that everything is OK, that we can go home now, that nothing is going to happen to us, we are free and that is it, and we went home.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: About what time of the day was that that you returned home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Around 6 o'clock in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did the villagers go back to their homes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did they stay in their individual homes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where did people gather?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In all sorts of different parts of the village. You know, for example, five or six family will gather in one house, one really strong house, you know, which had a basement or something, because people did not believe, they were still afraid that it can happen again.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Despite the fact that Cigo had said you could go home and you were free and everything would be OK?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When darkness fell, did anything happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, shelling started again.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where as the shelling directed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did the villagers attempt to flee this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, because, I mean, if you tried to do that, I mean, you do not know if you are going to get killed because there was no time to flee to that river again, because it just started immediately, they did not stop. So it was really, I mean, it was really risky to go outside and try to reach to that nearby river.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In large part, had the villagers selected, successfully selected strong homes to seek shelter and the homes in which the villagers were gathered, did they withstand the shelling?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The next morning were there more instructions from the Serb forces about what the villagers should do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What were you told?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They told us to gather our small basic things to take with us and that we are supposed to go to the same place as day before to that school, that buses were going to come and take us to Prijedor/Banja Luka or whatever, if we had relatives that we can stay there for a couple of days until they again clean the village from Muslim extremists.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did all the villagers gather to await the arrival of the buses and board the buses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, almost all, but I know two or three people left in the village, but those people were sort of ensured from Serbian, you know, people that nothing is going to happen to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was there anyone who had experience in a previous war who responded in a different way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The morning, that morning when they shelled the village, in the early morning of that day, also one of the World War II veterans, he hanged himself in front of his house because he told his sons that, you know, even though this is happening and even though they are saying we should go there, I mean, I know what is going to happen, I have been there once and I do not want to go through that same thing one more time. He just hung himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How many buses came to take the villagers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were coming in three or four buses, you know, some people, then coming back again or others.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So three to four buses would come, load up people, bring them to Prijedor and then return to pick up others?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you boarded one of the buses, where did it take you and the people you were with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They took us first to Prijedor but they did not take the highway, they took the old road. I know just one village, Tomasica, and all the rest of them. We came to Prijedor in the front of the sports hall.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you went through the old road on the way to Prijedor did you pass Serb villages?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we did and the people were standing outside, you know, cursing at us, throwing some stuff at us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After you arrived at the sports hall in Prijedor, were men separated from women and children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What ages of males were separated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From 15 to 60, male, were separated from other people.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were you and the other men who were separated from the women and children then taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To Brezicani.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is that Brezicani?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I am not sure if the same map we referred to earlier will show us where Brezicani is, but if we can look at it. Let me ask you, first, generally if Brezicani is located in the general area of Hambarine, so that one would starting from the Kozarac area or Kevljani area go past Prijedor to get to Brezicani?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: It is north-west on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I think that would be right. Miss Sutherland who has looked at this particular Exhibit advises me that she is not sure it is on that map and thinks it might be 280.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: B-R-E-Z-I-C-A-N-I.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That is north-west 79.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We have found it. The Judges have found it. Thank you. We have been looking at these maps for several months now, not all of them, so we are familiar with the Exhibits. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. [To the witness]: About what time did your group arrive at Brezicani?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was already dark, but the beginning of the dark or night fall.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where in Brezicani were you taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To one of those probably sports hall again.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where guards or soldiers waiting when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How were they positioned as you and the others left the bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we were leaving the bus towards the corridor, you know, from both sides and in front of the entrance of the hall were two small flash lights, I mean big flash lights, you know, and they were just towards us, to our faces. When we were leaving they were on both sides, when we leave the bus we were supposed to put our hands behind the head and run to the entrance into the hall. You know, they were just showing us the way, you know, beating, kicking, whatever they had in their hands, with the boots or with the hands, but, you know, to the hall.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were men from the villages around Kevljani already in the hall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was the nationality of those men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you entered were those men in a particular position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were. They were facing to the back wall on their knees, like sort of in our religion when you are praying, but only with the hands also behind their head.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you and the others who had just arrived also ordered to take that position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did people continue to arrive during the night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How long did you stay in that hall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In that hall?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Or in Brezicani?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That night and the following day and again until the midnight next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: At or around midnight were you again ordered to board buses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was the procedure for boarding the buses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The same way as getting in that hall, the same procedure, hurried out, beating until you get in the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After you boarded the buses where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They took us in front of Keraterm in Prijedor, and at that time there were already, I do not know how many, a lot of buses were already there filled with people. We just joined them and we started moving. At that time I did not know where we were going.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Eventually where did you end up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In mine in Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you arrive there at night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was happening as you arrived in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When my bus arrived, when we arrived we stopped and we did not leave the bus right away. From outside you could hear screaming, yelling, some occasionally shots, firing, I do not know to where or to whom. Then they told us to leave the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were Serb forces waiting when you got off the bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of those Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I recognised again Cigo was there and his army, I mean, the people who were with him in Kevljani when we were captured.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were those soldiers positioned in any particular way as you and others got off bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course. I mean they were also in the same way, in the corridor, just to the entrance to the building and all the way to my room.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Into what building were you taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Into the big building, this one here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If I can ask you to get up and use the pointer which is immediately to your right and show us the part of the building into which you were taken after you arrived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: OK. OK this is the main entrance. I turned left to upstairs through the hall into this ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: He needs to speak into that microphone so that the interpreters can hear. They are translating for Mr. Tadic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I entered through this door here. Then turned left upstairs through the hall into the last room in the back, the big one on the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So you enter that main entrance and then take the first stairway immediately to the left, and then once upstairs turn left in the hallway and down to the last room at the end?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you see a number written on the floor of that room?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you. As long as you are up, if we could get some assistance in removing the upper level of the model. Sir, would you later be held in another room in the hangar building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: OK. Can you show us where that room was located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the model]. Again through the main entrance, the second door, then turned right here and all the way until the room which is numbered A17.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: OK. Thank you very much. You can take your seat again. How many people were collected in the room at the far left end of the upstairs, in the far left end of the hangar building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Someone was trying to count the people, and I really do not remember the exact number, but I think somewhere 400 to 500 people.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What nationality were those people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslims the majority of them. I do not know if there were some Croats or other people, but the majority of the people were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you receive any food from camp authorities after your arrival?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not for first three days.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did interrogations of prisoners begin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you ultimately called for interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know how long after you arrived in camp that was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe 15 or 20 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After your interrogation where were you then held?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then they took me to that room I already showed, downstairs to A17 if I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is that the last room in the hangar in which prisoners were held?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It is not the last room but the last room where prisoners were.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Before you get to that room is there a room with a glass door which you can enter to get to another stairway?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you remain in Omarska until the main prisoner population was transferred to Manjaca or Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I remained there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Shortly before the main group of prisoners was transferred to Manjaca in Trnopolje, were you moved from room A17?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was. Five days before the majority of people left they sent me on the same ground floor in that hangar area. You do not exit the building from the ground floor. You just move more you up and that was the area where people were in.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: On the floor of the ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the floor of the hangar area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: --- of the hangar building itself. Can you show us generally where that area was, please? Again if you are going to speak you will have to remember to talk in the area of the microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The area was around here, A1. I was sleeping, you know, facing the wall, this wall here, with everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: OK. That was an area that had been wired in to accommodate prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After that when the main group of prisoners left, were you transferred for a brief time to another room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That day when they when the majority of people left that day, they took us, 173 people, and put us in what we called the garage and that is the room. We have to -- this is the room.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is that a small garage area ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, very, very small.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: --- in the restaurant building. How many prisoners were held in that room when you were there?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was that the group of people who remained in camp after the main prisoner population left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you then moved from that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were you held thereafter until you left the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In this room here just inside the garage, the big room, which is A5 or A4. A big room with wash rooms and the one hall down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I notice you are trying to read the numbers by looking through the model before its top portion is removed. Perhaps it would be easier if we took the top portion off so you can see the room in which you were held, and also the upper floor too, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was the main area where we were staying.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is there a number in that main area?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Can you talk into the microphone?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I am sorry, they may not have picked up what you just said. That was the main area where you were staying?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, that part.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You can resume your seat. Thank you. Were you and the other prisoners who were kept behind in Omarska after the main group of prisoners had been transferred, told that journalists would be coming to camp?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did the camp authorities instruct you what to say to those journalists?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What did they tell you to say in response to what kinds of questions?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Well, they asked you, for example, how long are you here, you are supposed to say, "not more than 15 days". They asked you how you have been fed, say, "four times a week". Is there any beating? "No." How do they treat you? "Very good." The reason why you are here? I do not remember that, either because of Muslim extremists or because I am a Muslim extremist.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You knew at the time but you are not sure what the correct answer you were instructed to give by the camp authorities is now?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were your rations of food increased?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, much, much better.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you and the other prisoners who remained behind ordered to clean up the camp?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What areas were cleaned up?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Almost all areas where the prisoners were kept.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: During that process did you have an opportunity to go into the white house?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you went into the white house what did you see? What was its condition?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: We were ordered to put the lockers inside the white house. So when we were taking them inside near to the floor in the corners on the walls you could see, you could see the piece of the skin, the hairs, you know, all blood somewhere just on the doors, and it was very hard to clean or to reach that or the first time a good job of cleaning it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Had the white house already been partially cleaned by that time?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, partially it was cleaned.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Those were parts of the white house that had not been completely cleaned in the attempt to do so?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, and in that area we were putting those lockers.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Velic, you indicated to us what the -- incidentally, do you recall which camp authorities instructed you and the others what to say to the journalists?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I do not remember which one of them were.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you recall ----

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Probably, you know, Zeljko Meakic the nearest charge there, but really I do not recall who said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was Zeljko Meakic's position in the camp?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: For my knowing, he was sort of commandant of that camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know what he did before the war?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, he was a policeman in Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You indicated to us what the camp authorities instructed you to say to journalists about conditions in the camp. Can you describe for us what in fact conditions were like in Omarska while you were there?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I mean, I cannot say terrible. You cannot really find a word for it, for those conditions. You know, every day, every night in that camp it was constantly beating, beating, killing. You could always hear the screaming, the beating. Wherever you go they beat. Even if you go, if you are lucky to get some meal that day, they were taking the people always out, taking them out, they would never come back. They would take the people from the room for the beating, then put him back in and tell him, for example, if he does not collect between us five or one thousand deutschemarks, that they are going to kill him, you know. They were doing that for a long time until the people ran out of the money. So then they started asking for the watches, for the, you know, if someone had a good jacket or something good. Constantly, every specially nights, nights were the worst when they were coming in and just open the door and you were just praying that they do not call your name out because if they call someone at night no one of those people ever came back.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What were hygiene conditions like?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Well, I mean, I can tell just for that time I never had a shower, brush my teeth or nothing. You had those lice, lice all over you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did the camp officials ever wash the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, they did. They probably, but most for the fun, they took us, you know, group by group outside. We had to take our clothes off to be naked, and then they would take big hoses with a very, very high pressure of water and pointing to us, and when that water hit you, I mean, you immediately fell, you could not get up. It was like someone really beating you very hard with that water, because at that time myself, I was really very weak. I lost weight. I did not have any movement, that much movement, you know, and my physical condition was terrible.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you say they probably did it for fun, was that amusement for the guards?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, they were just laughing because you cannot clean with that. They were just pointing those hoses in a group of 20 people, and, you know, they do not really -- you do not have time nothing to do. You just put your head in front of that water just kind of to save yourself from the hit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were particular groups or categories of prisoners at Omarska targeted for beating or murder?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, all those intellectuals or doctors, engineers, what we called at that time smart people. You know, people known for what they were before the war, had degrees or teachers, professors, they were targeted the most.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you ever learn, for example, what happened to the head of the SDA in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, I did. The time when I was in the room upstairs, in the last room upstairs, somewhere in the middle of the night I really had to go to the wash room. So I started knocking to the door and begging and begging them to open the door. I really wanted to. I was waiting there. I really had to go. So I was knocking on the door and begging and begging them for half an hour until they let me go. They let me go and then I went there and after that they told me I have to clean that whole wash room afterwards. So I did that and on my way back to the room one of the guards, they took me inside one of their rooms where they were stationed in that area upstairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That is in the hallway to the left of the first stairway?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes. There they started asking me the questions, what is my name, where I am from, and all that kind of thing. Then suddenly someone mentioned of them that Major Cehajic. I do not know for what reason. I just asked him, you know, is he here, you know. One of them told me: "Don't worry, we take care of him and he is gone." Nothing else. So that can mean a lot, but at that time it did not mean any good when they say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this might be an appropriate time.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will stand in recess until 2.30.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: (Luncheon Adjournment).

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, do you need Miss Sutherland? PRIVATE

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I believe I will. We can function without her, but if I might just have a moment to locate her?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: While Mr. Niemann has gone (but you can pass on), the Defence has filed a motion for protective measures, a recent motion for protective measures, and the Prosecutor has responded. The Trial Chamber considers that it would be important if we had a discussion regarding the Defence's motion and the Prosecutor's response. What we are proposing is that we do that after we finish with witness L. Since witness L will be in closed session, then we will just continue. Maybe we will begin with witness L, you think, this afternoon?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Then finish up tomorrow morning. But, in any case, when we finish with witness L, then we will hear arguments from counsel and comments regarding the motion for protective measures and the response of the Prosecutor. Now we are ready. We said that we were waiting for you, Mr. Niemann. Would you call Mr. Velic? MR. VELIC, recalled. Examined by MR. TIEGER, continued.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Mr. Velic, when we broke for the luncheon adjournment you had just described some of the general conditions in Omarska camp during the period of time you were there. While you were in Omarska camp, did you ever see Dule Tadic in camp?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In what part of Omarska were you when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: In the room on the ground floor hangar area, the last room where the people were.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: About how long after you were transferred to that room was it when you saw Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I do not really remember how many days, but it was not that many.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you remember what time of day it was that you saw him?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: It was afternoon, maybe just shortly afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Before you saw him had you heard anything happening outside your room?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, I heard some, you know, some kind of a noise like calling the names and something like that, but I did not pay too much attention to that because it was usual stuff there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether or not the door to your room was open or closed at the time those names were being called or that noise was happening from outside?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: They were closed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you recall any of the names you heard being called from outside?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I recall some, I am really not sure, but I think I heard something like some name "Alic" or something like that, but really I am not 100 per cent sure that that is exactly the one.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where in your room were you?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: In the back, just beside the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, might the witness be shown Exhibit 256? Sir, do you recognise that photograph as showing the room you were in?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: May that be placed on the overhead projector, please? Using the pointer, can you show us where you were in the room?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Right here. [The witness indicated on the photograph].

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: OK. So somewhat toward the right of centre as one looks toward the back of the room from the doorway area?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: OK. As shown in this particular photograph, just to the right of that table or bench shown in the middle of the wall?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In what position were you at that point?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: At that point I was leaning to the wall with my left shoulders or turned -- my face was turned to the wall, to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: OK. So you were standing up leaning against the wall?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: At some point after you had heard the sounds from outside, did the door to your room open up?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What did you do as the door was opening up?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: While the door was opening up, I just turned, turned, you know, straightforward to the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: OK. So with your back to the wall?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As you did that what did you see?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: While the door was opening and there was one of the guards opening the door, and while he was opening the door he was going with the door, so that he just leaned on the end of the door, and after that Dusko showed up in the front of the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I have this photograph marked next in order for identification, please? That would be 314. There are copies for the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: You are going to ask how the door opened, inwards or outwards, are you?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. [To the witness]: Sir, do you recognise this photograph as depicting your room shown from the inside looking toward the doorway?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I would tender this for admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: No objection. 314 will be admitted without objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Velic, in which direction did the door to this room open?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Well, the door was opening from outside and to the -- when I am looking to the door from inside, it is going to my right outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So as we are looking at the door now, the door would open out and toward the right?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You saw the guard opening the door and then standing at the end of the door?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Which would be to the right side?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And then Dusko Tadic in the doorway?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: We are not very clear which is the door. There are three partitions there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: OK. It may be clearer in the shot which is in the photograph itself which is now on the screen. But, sir, in what portion of that big door area was the actual door which opened? Can you point it out, please?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Where there is the open space here. [The witness indicated on the photograph].

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In this photograph can you make out the garage door on the other side of the hangar?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, from my -- from inside to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, as you look through the doorway here, can you see through the open doorway and see the garage door on the other side?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes -- not all but part of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you point to the portion where you see the garage door on the other side?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the photograph] Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you. The other portion, was that the only portion of the door which opened? Did any other portion of this large rectangular figure, dark rectangular figure, shown in the photograph open up?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: No, for the while I was there, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So that portion which is opened in this photograph was the doorway through which people entered and exited?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was Dusko Tadic doing in the doorway?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: He shows in the doorway. He, sort of, looked, you know, look all over us and people inside. Then he was looking all over us and, I mean, I did not look at him all the time, you know, and because, you know, I was exposed at that time, because I was standing in the back and I was really exposed because the rest of the people in the back, you know, in the middle, were all sitting. So I was the only one in the back standing so I was really exposed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So when you thought he might be looking at you, you looked down?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were any names called out?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What name was called out?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: "Jasko". Jasko's name, I do not know. I heard just "Jasko". I do not remember. I do not recall. I do not remember hearing a full name, first name or last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: OK. Were you looking at who called the name or were you looking down at that point?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I was looking down at that moment and I do not really know who called the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you know where Jasko's position in the room was?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Well, it was -- I mean, you can really see on this picture the wall and you entered from this extension of the wall. It was somewhere around here. Just there was one table beside the -- beside the wall and he was lying on that table.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: OK. Can we have Exhibit 257 for a moment, please? [To the witness]: Does Exhibit 257, the photograph you now have, show the portion of the room where the recess was?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Would that help you better indicate where Jasko's position in the room was?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you show us by pointing or explain using the photograph where Jasko was?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Well, just on the end of the picture here was the beginning of that table and, you know, going all the way. I do not know how long that table was, but maybe one metre or something like that long. So from here up to, you know, I do not know how long was the table, but from here to end of the table ----

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: OK.

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: --- beside the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When Jasko's name was called, did he respond?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You indicated to us that, as far as you knew, you were the only person standing at the back of the room. Do you know if people were standing in any other part of the room?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In what part of the room was that?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I can show you on just the picture that I saw before.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: OK, if you would, please?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: A couple of people were standing here, in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were there people sitting in the area near the door as well?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were they sitting?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: From all over, from the beginning when you enter the door on both sides and everywhere, from here, from here. Everything else was full.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: But, as far as you knew, you were the only person standing from, basically, the beginning of the room back?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you feel at that time conspicuous and exposed because of that position?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Of course I did. I mean, because whoever entered, you know, whoever comes to the door and looked inside the room, I would be the most exposed person in that room.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How long did it feel like you were standing there?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Well, it felt really like eternity for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you say to a Tribunal investigator that while you were standing there Dusko Tadic looked at the prisoners for two or three minutes?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, I remember saying that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you think that estimate was right?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Well, I do not think so. Because, like I said before, I mean, the place where I was and because I was exposed, for me, it really -- timing, I really could not time anything because, you know, I was just wondering about myself. For me, maybe it could be 15, 20 seconds but, like I said, it felt like eternity, but the two or three minutes, when I think a little bit more, it is not the right time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As you remained standing back there and continued and looked up and down or looked up now and then, did you continue to see Dusko Tadic in the doorway?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was it risky or dangerous to look up?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Well, of course it was, but I do not know, maybe the camp make me that, or I do not know what has happened in my head. Even though I know I am exposed and it is very dangerous to watch and, you know, my brain telling me, do not look, some part still -- still part of me still wants to see. You know, even though you are exposed and dangerous, still some part of me still wants to look. So, you know, I was always tried to put my, you know, my eyes down, but always I would just look, put, then look.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What would happen next?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Well, at that time when his name was called and even he did not answer, like I said, I do not know really time. I do not know timing, how much time he spent in the doorway. The door closed but not completely because, I mean, if you close the door completely and it was total silence inside the room, if you close the door completely, you could hear them, you know, shut. But the door was closed partially, I do not know how much, but it was closed partially, not all the way.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Could you see Dusko Tadic or the guard at that point?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Excuse me, I did not hear.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Could you hear and see Dusko Tadic and the guard at that point?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you take that opportunity to do anything?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, I took that opportunity just to slide down, to sit. You know, the same, where I was standing, I just, I would just slide down.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So you would blend in with the other prisoners?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Excuse me?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So that you would blend in with the other prisoners?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After you were on the ground, was there calling out again? Was Jasko called out again?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know how long after you slid to the ground it was that he was called out again?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I do not know the exact time, but not more than a minute or two.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Previously, you had been when you were standing, I take it you had an unobstructed view of the doorway?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now as you were seated at the rear of the room, you were behind many other prisoners, is that right?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you still concerned about looking at what was happening?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, I was but not the same way when I was standing. I mean, first of all, you know, I heard the name, it was not me, so, you know, I felt a little bit more comfortable, then plus I was sitting. So, you know, I was blocked. You know, they could not really see me that much while I was sitting. I was not exposed that much.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was what you were able to see from that position partially dependent on where people were in front of you and what kind of angle you had?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you look intermittently or look now and then after Jasko was called out the second time?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you look to Jasko to see if he was responding this time?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did he respond?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What did he do?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Well, he was lying on that table. He just get up and sit on the table. Then he, you know, stand completely. Then he put his jacket on, and then he starts making, you know, his way out through all the maze of people who were sitting down.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know why he put his jacket on?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Well, I mean, it was summer, so, you know, why? But probably just, you know, he thought that is going to help him if he was beaten again, you know, just not to hurt that much, you know, to have some kind of protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Had he been beaten before?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is that why he was on table?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, he was recovering. He was almost recovering because when I got in that room, he was -- when they send me in that room after investigation, he was laying. He could not get up. He was beaten.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did Jasko leave the room?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: During this time was your attention focused mainly on Jasko?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you able to see or do you recall whether or not the door had been opened all the way again ----

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Well .....

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: -- before Jasko got to the door?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, before he got to the door, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know who opened it?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you first notice the door before he got there or just about the point he was getting there?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Just about the point he was getting there because, you know, my eyes were going with him, you know. So while he was moving from his table, from his place, to the entrance, you know, I was just following him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you staring at him or just looking at him now and then?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Looking at him, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: At some point during this time that Jasko was called out and actually went out of the room, did you see Dusko Tadic again?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I think I saw him, but I cannot say 100 per cent it was him, because the place where I was, you know, but, you know, I cannot say 100 per cent, but I think I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You did not have the same unobstructed view that you had had when you were standing up?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As you have indicated, during most of this time you were looking at Jasko rather than the doorway?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: [Witness nods in assent].

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So the view you caught of the person you thought was Dusko Tadic on this occasion was brief?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Momentary? You were not 100 per cent sure as you were on the previous time that it was him?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you recall at what point in the process of Jasko getting out you saw the person you thought was Dusko Tadic? Was it just before Jasko left, as he was leaving the room or after he left the room?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: As he was leaving the room, maybe one, one and a half metre before the door, because in front of him there was people all over the place here and here, you know. So before you enter the door, everyone is sitting here, you have to, sort of, you know, not go straight but, you know, side way to get out.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: At some point after Jasko left the room was the door then again closed?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After he left the room could you hear sounds coming from outside?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Not immediately, maybe two minutes afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Then what sorts of sounds did you hear?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: First, the music was put on. Then you could hear the screams and unbelievable screams.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was that the sounds of people being beaten or tortured?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How long did that go on for?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: The time, I mean, also got really -- I mean it was, I never heard in my life before that kind of screams, especially mixed with that kind of music. For me, it felt, felt, very, very, you know, long, long. So, for me to say timing, how much, I mean, I can say maybe 15, 20 minutes, but I am not pretty sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You say there was music played. Do you recall what kind of music?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, it was one of, you know, from back from former Yugoslavia, one of the singers, like you call country music but, you know, local music, and song it was called "Let me live".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was Dusko Tadic wearing on this occasion when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: He was the wearing the uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What kind of uniform, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Those camouflage ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you remember whether or not he had any facial hair?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I remember, yes, he had some.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How much? I mean, can you indicate about how much or could you tell?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I mean, he had facial hair, full, but I do not mean completely full. I do not how old was that hair, but he had completely from here to all over the face.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: OK. Any idea how long was it?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: It is very hard to say. I mean, I do not know the people, how much time they need to grow the facial hair. Every person is different. So, by my estimation, it could be two weeks old.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Velic, can you tell us if you see Dusko Tadic here in court today?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you point him out, please, and tell us what he is wearing?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: That is the gentleman in the middle with the blue suit, the white t-shirt and the tie.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can the record reflect the identification of the accused, please?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, the record will reflect that the witness identified the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Nothing further, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Cross-examination, Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mr. Velic, the man you say was Dusko Tadic on this day in Omarska, did he look different from the Dusko Tadic that you had seen before the war?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Not really that I could not recognise him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Had you ever seen him with a beard before?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I do not recall. I do not remember if I see him or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you can think back to when you say you knew him in Kozarac, had you seen him with that same kind of beard that you have described as being worn that afternoon?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I mean, I tried, I mean, I tried to remember but really I could not, I could not remember, so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You were in this room with how many other prisoners?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: The number, really, I do not know but the room was crowded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Was it a full room so that people were cramped for space?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, especially at that time and afterwards, it was starting to become, it started to empty.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: As you have described the room, were most people sitting down?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You said there was a group of prisoners near the door who were standing up?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: A couple of people maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was anyone standing up on the other side of the door? If we look at Exhibit 314, the photograph of the door end of the room, you have it on the projector there?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: You mean to the left or to the right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Looking at the photograph, you describe people standing to the left, is that right?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: On the other wall where the hinge of the door would be, were there any people standing there?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So the people in front of the door were sitting down?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In that area did the people in the room go up to the foot of the door, to the actual door frame?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes. The first man was right here. [The witness indicated on the photograph].

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: As we see that big metal sheet which spans across the wall from the side to about two-thirds of the way along the front of the room, were people up against that metal sheet that we see in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: You mean this part here?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That door that we see in the photograph opens outwards into the hangar itself?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, I mean, it opens to -- yes, to outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The hinges, as we look at the photograph, would be on the right-hand side on the wall side of the door, is that right?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Can you repeat that again?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: As we look at this photograph ----

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: From inside?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- yes, the hinges would be on the right-hand side of the door by the wall?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: You mean this small part here?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The lighting in this room only came from some windows against the back wall?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: During the day and at night we had -- we had sometimes the power on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: At this time in Omarska there was no light, was there, in this room, no electric light?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Sometimes we had, yes, we had.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thinking about this afternoon, in particular, was there an electric light or not in this room?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I do not think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we can look at that photograph that showed the back of the room again, Exhibit 256, we see there the source of natural light into the room, do we not?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That glass for the most part is a kind of opaque glass, is that not right?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, it looks like it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It is not a clear glass through which you can clearly see outside, it is a kind of thick cloudy glass?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I would not say cloudy but thick, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It is not what we are used to looking out through our ----

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Of course not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- house windows.

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Of course not. It depends if you have them or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, it conceals a view outside if you attempted to look through that window?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You, presumably, had occasion when you went into the main hangar, the main garage, which exists outside this room, is that right?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I do not know if you can remember what date or month or in relation to your period of time at Omarska when it was that this afternoon took place?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: No, I really could not tell any exact day or date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Right. Outside this room and in the main hangar, again that was an area that was not lit by electric light?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: During the day, no, I do not think so, but they occasionally opened those big garage doors in the back ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: -- so you had lights, daylight inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. But this is a particular room that is further down the building, is it not? It is towards the end of the building and the shutters, as we can see from the model, how many shutters left before you get to the end of the building? You can see better than me from where you are.

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I think you have the one room after that and that big part.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, so there is one shutter, is there not, opposite this door?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I really do not ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: OK. Those shutters were occasionally opened by the guards to allow natural light into the garage?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, you mean in the hangar itself -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. But this hangar was filled with all sorts of equipment that were connected with the mine, for instance, dumper trucks?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, but as I recall, I saw only one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Opposite your door to that particular room, can you remember what was at the back of the hangar there towards the shutters?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I could saw some things there, but not that -- I mean, some sort of metal things but not that high, you know, some -- whatever they used in the mine ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: --- at that time and I could see the part of that door, garage door, which was opening.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are you saying then that the garage door opposite this door was open on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: No, no, on that occasion, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No. Did you have occasion yourself to go out of the room during that afternoon?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: No, because we were not allowed to go without first getting permission from them to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In the course of that morning did you go out of that room, perhaps, to go to the toilets which were nearby?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I went to the lunch.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: At lunch time?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Well, lunch time was, you know, you can go at 8 o'clock if you are first or you can go at 6 o'clock if you are last.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember when you had been out of that room or if you had been out of that room earlier in the day?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, I have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What time would that have been?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Maybe around 10.00, 11.00. It was before afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Before the afternoon. Were there any guards in the hangar at that time?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: On that afternoon, were you aware of what guards were on duty and, if so, to whose shift they belonged?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I do not know to whose shift. I mean, I forgot. Before I knew. I mean, it was a very, very long time since that happened. I knew almost every shift, who was their leader. But that day I really do not know what shift was and who was the head of that shift. I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: From that position where you were at the back of the room, did you recognise the guard who came to the door, first of all?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Had you seen him before?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Maybe I saw him, but I really did not pay too much attention to him because he was just one of the guards, especially if he does not do -- you know, have those guards who were doing a lot of bad things, so you paid a little bit more attention to them than to those who did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You told us that it was the guard who opened the door, first of all?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did the guard come into the room?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How far did the guard open the door?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: All the way, I mean, all the way until -- the door was open, if I can show the just picture before, if you want me?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Exhibit 314, please?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I do not know if the door can go all the way to the -- when you open it all the way to the back hall and outside, but the door was open just for the doorway. [The witness indicated on the photograph]. You could see somewhere here, you know, him leaning on the end of that when you open the door and then you have that part of the door. You could see him leaning on that part of the door. I mean, half part of his body.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. So the guard was leaning against the door and, as we saw on the photograph, with his back near the part where the hinge would be, is that what you were indicating?

utterances.speaker: A9
