utterances.text: I just see half of his body leaning, I mean, and looking at us, you know, just with, you know, occasional looks, looks, you know, facing behind Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When the guard opened the door, did he say anything to the room?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: No, not, not -- he did not say anything when he opened the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was there just the one name called out, "Jasko"?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: That is what I remember. Maybe they called some more, but I am really not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Who called out the name "Jasko"?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I do not know. I was not looking at that time to them, you know, who opened their mouth or what, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So it seems when you were leaning against the wall and, as you said, you were at risk, you were exposed, that you were conscious that you did not want to expose yourself to the attention of that guard?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, of that guard and Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, and so what you were doing against that wall was glancing up for short moments, to risk viewing what was happening by the door?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, I mean, I was just, you know, look, then put my eyes down and then I again look and put it down. So, I do not know if that is glancing or short looks, but something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What you are talking about there is movements that last for a second?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, but for me that second really did not felt a second, for me at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But that is all it was as you were showing us then, just casting your eyes up and then down to the ground?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Not completely down, I mean, put my head down, I just put my eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, but ----

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: But yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- when you are looking down at the ground you are not looking at the door?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You spent longer looking at the ground ----

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I do not think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- than you did the door?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I do not think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You do not think so?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I did not, no. I did not. I spend much time looking at the door than to the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I mean, are you just saying that because you want to try to accuse Dusko Tadic in relation to this incident that happened in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: No, I am not saying that. I am here just to say what I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Have you picked up a story here that you have heard from other prisoners in Omarska and in Manjaca where you went as a prisoner later on?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Did I pick up the story?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: No, no. I just came here with my knowledge of that day, what I saw personally, without any other people telling me what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You have been asked by Mr. Tieger about the statement you made to the Tribunal's investigators on 22nd March this year?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is that right?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: My first statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Maybe it was. I do not know what date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you would like to have a look at it, we can show you the date. I tender here D32, your Honour. Yes. This is your statement in English that was signed by you and dated, as you will see on page 4, 22nd March of this year.

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Well, then probably it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You have signed it just above there ----

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, if I signed it ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mr. Velic.

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: --- if I signed this statement -- I mean, I do not really now recall the date when Mr. Tieger was with him. But if this is my signature and it was given on 22nd March, then it is.

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: 6, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I mean, if you would you like to look at every page, you will see that every page is signed by you.

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, I know. I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Not also me, the interpreter and Mr. Tieger and .....

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You were spoken to with a police officer present at the time, is that right?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I was -- on the same day?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: A police officer?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you look at the foot of the statement there on the front page -- we do not need the name mentioned now as we have tried to avoid identifying people -- you will see someone with initials?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Excuse me, but this was not my interview with Mr. Tieger, as you said. This is with Thomas, Mr. Thomas. So that happened before, before I spoke with Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. You spoke on 22nd March of this year?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: But not with Mr. Tieger, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: (Indecipherable).

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Let us look then at what you said ----

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: OK.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- because it was only a few months ago, was it not?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But almost four years after these events that you have told us about?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: [The witness nods in assent].

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Had you given anyone a statement before 22nd March of this year?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I remember giving one when they came to the country I am stationed now, but that was just some kind of brief ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: --- a brief statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Right. Did it deal with the events that you have described here?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Not in details, no, just globally what happened back ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: --- in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was it a description of what had happened to you in Bosnia and conditions in Omarska, was it, just a general ----

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Just general things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. So would it be right to say the first time you were asked to specifically recall these events was in March of this year?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you were thinking back nearly four years later, did you have difficulty remembering who you had seen and what had happened?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I did not have problem with who I had seen. I had problem only with dates and dates most of the time and timing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You might like to turn to page 3 then of that statement ----

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: OK.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: -- because you speak English very well and, obviously, can you read English?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. You will see in that statement in the third paragraph of page 3 that you recall, "I know for sure that he called out 'Jasmin' nickname 'Jasko' and 'Alic', first name unknown"?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You seem to have recalled then that when Dusko Tadic came into the room he called out two names?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, at that time I said that, but the problem was that the day before Mr. Thomas came I was working night shift, 12 hours. I did not get any sleep. My head was not really clear and that was, as you said, after four years and I had to give in short time, you know, a statement. So I really, afterwards when they left and after I was thinking more about, I said some -- I said some things, I mean, like I said about the second name, which I ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Alic?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: --- which I was not sure afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Or is it the case that you have heard evidence that has been given during this trial, that you know what other witnesses have said?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: No, because the country I am stationed really did not pay too much attention to this trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Or has anyone told you what other witnesses have said?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Because Eno Alic was in the room upstairs above yours?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Probably he was, I do not know. You told me that. No, I did not even know where he was. So that is the first time I hear where he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But you said then, in March 1996, that he was called out with Jasko from your room?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Like I said, after thinking afterwards, you know, after my statement, after, you know, little bit more of thinking and trying to remember, you know, what has happened, I really -- I really was not sure that was true what I said about Alic. Like I said now to Mr. Tieger, you know, I am not sure. I did not want to say that he called "Alic" also because I cannot say really he called him that day, because I am not sure any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So do you think that your memory concerning this incident that afternoon in Omarska is faulty, that you have made mistakes?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: On the part of the -- which concerned the Jasko and seeing Dusko Tadic that day, it is not faulty. I know that for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Have you discussed this incident with anyone else, any other witness?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: You mean during this trial now?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Not during this trial but after it took place, did you discuss this incident with anyone else who claimed to have been there?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, I mean, I was -- it was, you know, stories around. I was trying to ask the specific, the specific man, witness G.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: And I tried, you know, to ask him some specific details, but he, like I said, he just told me which I already knew, that was Mr. Tadic there and he did not want to go in any detail, so .....

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did not witness G claim that Tadic had killed them?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: That is what he told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: And I did not see that, so I cannot tell Mr. Tadic killed him or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is that why you indicated the name of Enver Alic ----

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: -- or Alic, and why you are claiming that Dusko Tadic was there when Jasko was called out of that room?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Because that day I saw Dusko Tadic at that door. That is what I know for fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Another thing, why in March 1996 did you say in that statement that he, meaning Dusko Tadic, then called out the names of the two prisoners?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I have already told you that my circumstances before that statement, I had no time to prepare myself for that statement. I was tired, and I had to give that statement in a very short period of time. Maybe I put some things I did not mean to say, but just went out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you often do that, say things you do not mean to say?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Say things that are totally different from what they were?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Velic, let me just to try to clarify something that Mr. Kay asked you about. I think he said that you said in your statement that Enver Alic was called out of your room. If you look at your statement, is it not true that you told the investigator that you had heard the name "Alic" being called as you remembered on that particular day when you were interviewed, but that you did not remember him leaving with Jasko and he could have been in another room?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, I mean, as I told you when you asked me a question about hearing any noise before the door opened, I told you that I might have heard the name "Alic", so on that day when I gave this statement, maybe I did not really think that clearly like now about this. Maybe on that day, you know, I said instead of I heard that name or something like that before the door opened outside, I just put it that I heard here inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: There was also a suggestion that you mentioned the name "Alic" because G told you that Dule Tadic had killed Mr. Alic. Does your statement not indicate that G told you that Tadic had killed "Jasko" and "Karaba" but did not specifically mention Enver Alic?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Just very quickly with respect to the position of the guard who opened the door: as you indicated on the photograph when the door was open, it was roughly parallel to the right wall?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: OK. If I understood your gesture correctly, was the guard leaning against the edge of the open door with half his body out of view and the other half of the body -- so his front was leaning against it ----

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: --- and half his body out of view and half his body in view? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is all I have. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, nothing arises. I have tendered D32 which I offer as an Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: D32 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Witness, you spoke at the beginning of your evidence about leaving the army, the JNA, before your time was up. This seems to have been something that happened a good deal with non-Serb members. Were you in danger after that of being arrested as a deserter or were they glad to see non-Serbs go?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: No, not really. I spent three months after that at home. Really no one did not even, even my Serbian neighbour, they knew I escaped from army, you know, so I mean no one really bothered me. No one really asked me why. No one really gave me any hard time or trying to catch me or put me somewhere. So my feeling was that they were really glad we left.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: To your own knowledge, this happened a great deal with non-Serb members of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Of course, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: The only other question I wanted to ask you, your ID that you had in common with everyone else's ID would show your nationality, would it?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: My ID?

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I mean -- you mean the army?

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: No, as a civilian, Yugoslav citizen.

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, I mean, not -- when I was in the primary school, I mean, I never, or in the high school, I never said when I was signing the paper or something like that, and it is the question of nationality, I was always write down Yugoslavian and that is Muslim.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: But on your ID what would it show?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Now?

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: No, then just before the war?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: "Yugoslavian" because, I mean, most of the Muslim people at that time, they were all expressing themselves as a Yugoslavian.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Not Bosniak?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Not that I remember, no.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Thank you. One question just perhaps following from that: do you know whether most Muslim people's IDs would show that they were Muslim or would most of them just say "Yugoslav"?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I do not really know for all the people.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: You do not know?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: People that you know?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I mean, I know for ordinary people that were writing down that they were Yugoslavian all the time. I mean, from my father, from my mother and all my relatives (and I have a great deal of relatives around), they were all writing down as Yugoslavian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Velic what was the size of Kevljani -- is that the way you pronounce it?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Thank you. What was the population about of Kevljani at the time of the attack in May 1992?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: The population of the people?

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: How large was it?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Well, the village was very spread, you know. I mean, it was not really -- you know, it was almost house by the house. But some, you know, you had a house and you had some people were, you know, in their fields, owning the fields, or some kind of property, then another house. Actually, the village was divided in three parts. The village we called Kevljani, you have also after that a town called Hadzici which was belonging to us as a community, but, you know, it is just a different name.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: So the community of Kevljani would be, you cannot give me an approximation of the size?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I mean, the community of Kevljani includes Kevljani, Hadzici, Jakupovici, upper and lower, and it is very hard -- it was big, big area. It was big area.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: What was the predominant religion of the community, if you know?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Religion?

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Islam.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Muslim?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, Muslim.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger? Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Nothing arises, your Honour. Mr. Tieger, do you have any questions? I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was the date on which you left the army and returned to Kevljani, the approximate date?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: The date? When I left the army?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, and returned to Kevljani?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: December 31st 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection to Mr. Velic being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Velic, you are permanently excused. You are free to leave. Thank you for coming

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann, who is your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The next witness is L, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. We will stand in recess then until 4 o'clock.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: (Closed session) [Confidentiality partially lifted by order of the Chamber]

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We are in closed session now. Good. Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. I call witness L. Before I do so, your Honour, I notice there are some people in the booth up there. I do not know whether they are connected with the Tribunal in any way?

utterances.speaker: MISS FEATHERSTONE
utterances.text: In the French booth?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, in the technical booth.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. They are not connected with the Tribunal but ----- A TECHNICIAN: It is Dutch security.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: They probably know the witness anyway, if that is the case. OK, your Honour. I call witness L. WITNESS L, called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Sir, would you take the oath, please, that is being handed to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Would you read that oath, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Excuse me just one minute. Mr. Niemann, you may continue. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Witness, I can ask you to look at this piece of paper and if you can tell me whether your name appears on the paper. Might the paper be shown to the Defence before showing it to the witness?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Witness, in October of 1992 were you 16 years of age?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you and your family live in north western region of Bosnia adjoining the Croatian border?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you subsequently in October 1992 move with your parents to an area near to Trnopolje in the opstina of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Are you by nationality a Serb?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was your occupation prior to the war in 1992 a school student?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Why did you and your family move to the opstina of Prijedor in October 1992?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Because of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What particular aspect of the war caused you to move?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: We could not be in that area because there were Serbs of ethnic descent, and Muslims were all attacked from the Bosnian side by the Fifth Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were you called up into the army in October 1992?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you respond to the call-up notice?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you join the army?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: No, I was not in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Why did you not join up in the army at that time?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Because I was under age and I am sorry, Mr. Niemann and your Lordships, I was a minor and I was not in the regular army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: In October 1992, did your family obtain accommodation in a town near Trnopolje in the opstina of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Had you ever been to this place before this date?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you arrived at this place had the original occupants left? Had they left by this stage?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Excuse me. I did not quite hear the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you arrived at this place where your family obtained accommodation, had a large number of the original occupants left the place?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did other Serb refugees from north western Bosnia also come to this place where your family obtained accommodation about the same time as your family came there?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know some of the people that came to this place as refugees? Do you know the names of some of the people?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Are you able to name some of them?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you do it now?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, (redacted), Josip Popovic, Zoran Ergarac, Dragan Maric and others -- many Serbs from my area who had moved to Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were there other Serb refugees at this place already there when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were these refugees receiving humanitarian aid?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know where humanitarian aid was being distributed from?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: It was distributed in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know who was responsible or in charge of distributing the humanitarian aid in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: From what we knew, it was Dusko Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know where the supplies of humanitarian aid were coming from that were being distributed?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: As far as I knew, it was brought over from Prijedor, but it was brought in by the United Nations.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How did you know that it was coming in from the United Nations?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: They otherwise brought this aid, because they were in that area of Yugoslavia, of Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see the United Nations operating in this area delivering supplies and humanitarian aid?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: In Kozarac, do you know where this humanitarian aid was being distributed, what part of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: It was distributed not far from the petrol station in Dusko Tadic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you describe the property, the house from which it was being distributed from?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: That house had was a one storey building. There was a shop and a coffee bar of the white colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was your family in receipt of humanitarian aid when you lived in Prijedor, the Prijedor opstina?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you go to get humanitarian aid on behalf of your family?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Approximately, when was it that you went to get this aid?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: That humanitarian aid was distributed around the 22nd October.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Who did you go with when you went to get humanitarian aid for your family?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: To (redacted), from the same area that I came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: You knew this person prior to coming to the opstina of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you went to get humanitarian aid, who did you see at this place?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I saw Dusko Tadic who was sitting at a table and receiving the cards from the International Red Cross with our names on them, with the names of refugees, and all the families and all the members of those families were written down so that they would be entitled to receive the humanitarian aid.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were you introduced to Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Who introduced you?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Other than just being introduced, did you have a conversation with Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Sorry -- no.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: For how long were you at the premises on this day, do you remember, approximately?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Sorry, you were in the house -- we were receiving the humanitarian aid.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, how long were you there?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: About 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: During this period of 15 minutes, did you see Dusko Tadic at the house?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you describe what you remember of his physical appearance on that day?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: He was clean shaven, clean, big. He had civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you remember the colour of his hair?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: He had black hair, curly with sideburns.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you notice whether or not he was armed or carried any weapons?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: He was not armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see him there with anyone else?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: There was an unknown woman whose family name was not known to me, but there was a female whose first name was "Branka".

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did someone tell you what position Dusko Tadic held in the town of Kozarac at that time?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Sorry, I do not quite understand this word "position". Excuse me. What position? I do not quite understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did someone tell you what job Dusko Tadic held in the town of Kozarac at this time?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Well, he distributed the humanitarian aid, seemed to be responsible for the International Red Cross, and he was one of the armed who was a Commander in the camp at Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Who told you this?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: That he was a Commander in the camp?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, who told you this, gave you this information?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: It was given me by Bosko Dragicevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: After you collected the humanitarian supplies, where did you and (redacted) go?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: We were in the restaurant in the same house. It was in the same house but elsewhere, in other part.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What did you do in this other part?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: We sat down there. There were people gathering there where drinks would be taken out, where Bosko Dragicevic was there and a policeman by the name of Ljuban.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you know Bosko Dragicevic?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: You mean before?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: So is this the first time that you met him?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you tell me how old he was, approximately?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Who, sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Bosko Dragicevic.

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: He was about 40.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you from the conversation find out where he came from?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Bosko Dragicevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: From what I learned in the talk with me and (redacted), he was from the area of Kozarac and that he also lived in the area of Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you also find out what his job was?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: That he was also a policeman -- sorry, a civilian policeman, but otherwise he was a policeman who worked at the Trnopolje camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: At that time were you interested in getting a job?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, because the mobilization of Serbs was underway of those who had crossed into the territory of the municipality of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did (redacted) know that you wanted a job, that you needed a job?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Did -- excuse me, I could not hear it very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did (redacted) know at the time that you wanted to obtain a job?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: He was -- he knew already that I needed a job because of the mobilization. Otherwise, in his conversation he asked Bosko Dragicevic whom he had known for quite some time whether there was a possibility for me, whether there was a vacancy where I could be employed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where was this vacancy at? Where was the job to be at?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: You mean where I got a job?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, where were you to work? What was the discussion about in terms of where you would work?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: During that discussion it was said that I could get a job at the Trnopolje camp as a guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did they discuss the income you would earn?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you also find out that other Serb refugees that had come from north western Bosnia were also working at this camp?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did they tell you to whom you were to report for this job when you started?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Who did they say you should see?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I went first to Josip Popovic and then with him I went to Trnopolje, to the camp, where Bosko Dragicevic was at the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When did you go to the camp, to the Trnopolje camp? How long after this meeting on 22nd October 1992 did you then go for the first time to Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Excuse me. I did not hear it very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When did you go first, when was your first day, can you remember the date, the first day you went to the Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: On the 26th October '92.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you go there on that day with Josip Popovic, as was originally planned?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Before that I went with Josip Popovic. Excuse me. On 25th of October '92, I went with Josip Popovic to Bosko Dragicevic's office which was next to the Trnopolje camp. Then there I was issued a uniform and Dragicevic took me out from that office and then went to show me various facilities, the sentry posts which were in the Trnopolje camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where in relation to the camp was the office of Bosko Dragicevic?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Excuse me, if -- let me explain. If you come from the direction of Kozarac to Trnopolje, it is on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Perhaps you could assist us more. What side of the road was the main part of the camp, as you came from Kozarac towards Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: On the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you arrived at the camp and you were being shown around by Bosko Dragicevic, did you recognise any of the camp guards that you saw there?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Are you able to give the names of any of those camp guards that you recognised?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Well, as far as I can recall, there was Zoran Ergarac, Sinisa Popovic, Dragan Maric and some other policemen who worked there. They were all in the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you recognise these guards as being people that had come from the same region as you had come from?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were these also young men like yourself, these men that you have just named?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: They were a little bit older than I am, some my age. There were some that were older than I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What were the conditions in the camp like when you first saw it?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: When I arrived, when I walked around with Bosko Dragicevic, they were very terrible.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you say "terrible" are you talking about the condition of the hygiene of the camp or the accommodation or what, can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Approximately, how many prisoners were there at that time, were you told that?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: There were about 1500, in my estimate, who were within the camp, who were in the dom and the school building.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What was the prison population of the camp made up of mostly?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: You mean who were, what sort of -- I apologise, you mean the hygiene of the people?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, no. Can you tell us, was the camp population women and children and old men?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Women and children and elderly people, they were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see many men of military age? By "military age", I mean from 17 through to 50?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: They were not 17 to 50. They were 55 to 80, more.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know the religion or nationality of the people that were in the camp?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Nationality?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did Dragicevic tell you when you could commence work?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When did he say you would start work?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: He told me that I could start the next day, that was October 26th 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I think you said a moment earlier that you were issued with a uniform?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you describe the uniform that you were issued with?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: The uniform was SMB in colour, which is the shirt and trousers and a pullover and there was a multi-colour police uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you report for duty the next day, that is, 26th October 1992?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What time did you get to work?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I arrived in the morning at around 7 o'clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you again meet with Dragicevic?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did he introduce you to the guard that you were to relieve?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I knew that guard myself, except that I came to this guard post and he gave me his rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What was that guard's name? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I cannot quite remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you remember what guard post you were to work at?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I was at the guard post No. 4 which was next to the asphalt, to the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you say next to the asphalt, to the road, what part of the camp was it? Can you tell us a little bit more about where it was located?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: It is in the front part of the camp which is where the road is from Kozarac to Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were you told what your duties would be as a guard at the camp with respect to handling the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What was your job? What were your duties?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: My job was not to allow the civilians from the other side to go and mingle with the people and the other military which is moving towards the positions, and not to approach these inmates and also the inmates not to climb the fence, so that they could not get out.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Is there a railway station near Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How far from the camp is the railway station, roughly, approximately?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Well, it is -- you mean the way the crow flies? I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: If you had to walk there, how far you would have to walk, approximately, from the camp itself to the railway station?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: About 60 to 70 metres from the camp to the railway station.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you tell me what buildings went to make up the camp?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, I can. There was a school building, a store, the dom, one large shed and there was also an electric substation and, I am sorry, there was also a built latrine, an outhouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was there open ground around the camp itself?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I am sorry. I did not hear the question very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was there a field around the camp, around the buildings, an open area of land?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: It was fenced.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: You mentioned your guard post No. 4. How many guards posts were there?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How many were there altogether, in total?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Four.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where were they positioned, can you tell us? Where were the four guard posts positioned?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: They were at the corners of the objects of the school building, between the store and towards the railway station, and there were two on the road that led from Kozarac to Trnopolje. There were two behind that leading towards the soccer field, towards Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: From what you could see, where for the most part were the prisoners kept?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: The women and children were kept in the primary school building, and the elderly were in the dom.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where were the prisoners' toilets?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: They were between the school building and the dom, towards the road that leads to Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were they enclosed in a building or were they out in the open?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: They were open.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was there running water supplied to the prisoners at the camp?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did they have beds to sleep on?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What was the cleanliness of the camp? Was it cleaned up on a regular basis or was it left dirty?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: It was all dirty.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you know a guard at the camp by the name of Zoran Karajica?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know, approximately, how old he was?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: He was 20 to 25 years old, 25.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not he was Serb, or was he some other nationality?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: As far as I knew, he was Catholic, of catholic faith, Catholic faith.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know where he came from?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Zoran Karajica?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: From Trnopolje. His house was not far from the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you were at the camp, did you also know a guard by the name of Milan Cavic?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Again, approximately, how old was Cavic?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Somewhere 30, between 35 and 40 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know where he came from?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: From the part of -- from around Omarska, Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know what nationality he was?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: A Catholic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: A few days after you started work at the camp, around the end of October 1992, did you see Zoran Karajica and Milan Cavic go into the office of Bosko Dragicevic?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you remember about what time of the day this was?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: When they came to the office of Dragicevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, roughly, if you can remember. You may not remember.

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Somewhere around 11.00, maybe noon. I could not tell you exactly, but it was around noon.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you then see these men go into one of the buildings in the camp?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Shortly after that, did you see them leading out four elderly prisoners?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I wonder if my learned friend would refrain in leading in relation to evidence we are about to deal with?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I will sustain your objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Shortly after, what happened then?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: They entered the camp and after some time they went into the dom from where they took out four elderly men.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When they brought out these elderly men, were these men tied up in any way or were they just walking freely with the guards?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Their hands were tied behind their backs.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Approximately, how old were these prisoners?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I cannot recall exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were they men in their middle age, I am talking men in their 50s, or were they older than that?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: As far as I remember, all were between 55 and 80. I do not know exactly how old those were that were taken out had.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How were they being led out of the building?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: They were holding them under their arms. They were tied behind their backs, but they were holding them under their arms. They took them out of the dom, out of the school building -- no, out of the dom and walked them across the street and took them to a white house.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you say "they", who was it that was holding and leading these men?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Zoran Karajica and Cavic, Milan Cavic, and Bosko Dragicevic followed them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see whether or not Bosko Dragicevic was carrying any weapons or arms?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, he had an automatic rifle with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I think you said a moment ago they took them in the direction of a white house. Where was this house located from where you were?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: That house was to the right across from the road in the direction of Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: From what you could see of it, did you know whether or not the house was occupied?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: In the white house?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Had somebody lived there previously?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No. I am asking you was somebody living in the house at the time when you were in the camp?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: No, nobody lived in that house.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you recall what date this was that you saw these men being led out of the co-operative building?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I do not remember. Sorry, do I?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you recall the date, do you remember what date, it was when you saw these four men being led out of the co-operative building?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: That was the first day, October 26th, when I started working.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: You saw them take these men towards that building that you said was a white house. Where did they take them to, could you see?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I am sorry, I do not know that my sound system -- I understand Mr. Niemann, but on listening there is a bit of a problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see where they took these men to?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I am sorry. OK.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see ----

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, could you?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see where they took these men to?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: They took them in the direction of the white house, of that white house.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see what they did with the men?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: From my vantage point, from my guard post, I watched and they took these men to the white house and there was a pole there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What did they do then?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: They tied them up to that pole and after a while Bosko Dragicevic shot at those old men and, as far as I could tell and from my point of view, those old men were all killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: After they were shot at, what did they do then, did you see?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: They left them on that pole. They returned to the office, the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: While this happened, did you have an uninterrupted clear view of the event and what occurred, or were there obstructions that were in your road?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I could see a lot of what was going on because my view was clear all the way to the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: After these men had been shot, did Karajica, Cavic and then Dragicevic come back?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: To the command?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Later on in that day did you see Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: About what time of the day was it when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: That was part of the day before the evening, before my shift changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where did you see him?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: He arrived in his Golf to Trnopolje where the house was that was the command, and he came to Bosko Dragicevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did he go into Bosko Dragicevic's office?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: He walked inside, but I did not know where he was in the office, was he in Dragicevic's or his own.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did he arrive with anyone else or was he by himself?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: He arrived with Zoran Ergarac who was taking over my shift.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see Dusko Tadic again later that day or was that the only time you saw him?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: It was the only time I saw him there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Some days later, did you again see Dusko Tadic at the camp?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you remember when it was, the next time you saw him, approximately, the date?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I cannot quite recall the date, but he came the next day also in his Golf to the command and met with Bosko Dragicevic and a couple of policemen where Zoran Karajica and Milan Cavic were, and then after a while they went into the dom in the camp, and then in the meantime Dusko Tadic was in that camp and then came out of the camp and they brought out 10 inmates from the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you remember what time of the day this was? Was it in the morning or in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Well, in the morning, somewhere around, I cannot say exactly, but in the morning around 8.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did Dusko Tadic himself enter the camp compound when they collected these 10 men?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Once they collected the 10 men, these 10 men were prisoners, were they?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Once they collected these 10 men, what did they then do with them?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Tadic went in his Golf towards Kozarac and Bosko Dragicevic, Zoran Karajica and Cavic and some policemen remained.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did they do anything with the 10 men that they had gathered up from the camp?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: They took them towards the white house and after half an hour they came back. I did not hear any shots. I did not see those 10 prisoners who had been taken out to return, and I assumed that those people had their throats slashed behind that house where there was a garden.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you said "they returned", do you mean that the guards returned?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, the guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: From what you could see Dusko Tadic merely got in the vehicle and drove away?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see Dusko Tadic again that day at the camp?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: That day?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you recall the 5th November 1992?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were you working at the camp on that day?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What time did you arrive at the camp to start your work on that day?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: We came around 7 o'clock in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Shortly after you arrived at work on that day, did you see Milan Cavic and Zoran Karajica go into the office of Bosko Dragicevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Again I would ask my learned friend not to lead on these matters, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I will sustain your objection. Mr. Niemann, please rephrase your question without leading. "Did you see anyone go into his office and, if so, whom?"

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: At about 7 o'clock that day did you see someone go into the office of Bosko Dragicevic?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Who did you see go into the office of Bosko Dragicevic?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: There were Zoran Karajica, Milan Cavic and after a while Dusko Tadic arrived with his car.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What did Dusko Tadic do when he arrived at the camp?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: He was in his office, came out with that Bosko Dragicevic, Zoran Karajica, Cavic. They entered the dom. Sorry, excuse me, they entered the camp and they reached the school and after some short time they took out a girl whose hands were tied behind her back.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What was Dusko Tadic doing while this was happening?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: He was at the entrance to the elementary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What did Dragicevic do?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: You mean Bosko?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, Bosko Dragicevic.

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: They were inside the school and then they brought out the girl.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: After they brought out the girl, what did Bosko Dragicevic do?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: They brought out a girl and took her between dom and the shop and started with her, to take her out on to the asphalt. Dusko Tadic followed Cavic and Zoran Karajica. Bosko Dragicevic came to me and told me to follow him, to go with him, that he needed me. He took my rifle off my shoulder and started and I asked him how could I leave my sentry post, how was I to leave my sentry post.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you asked him that, what did he say?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: He told me that I could feel free to leave, that that sentry post would be covered by Sinisa Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: So I left with him. He took my rifle. We went out of the camp. I did not know what it was all about. Dusko Tadic was following Zoran Karajica and Cavic alongside that girl, behind that girl, behind those who were taking that girl along. They brought her to the white house. Bosko Dragicevic asked me if I had ever had any sexual intercourse with a female person, with a girl, how shall I say it. I said no and that I would not like ever to have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What did he then say to you?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: He told me not to worry about that, that he would make it possible for me even if by rape.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When he said "even if by rape", what did you say to him about that?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I told him that I would not like to do that because I had a mother and my sister and I would not like anything happen to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What did he do then? What did he say then?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: He did not say anything to me. He said to follow him. He took me by my shoulder and then we started off. We reached a house with a cellar. We entered that cellar in which there were Dusko Tadic, Zoran Karajica and Milan Cavic with the girl.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you go down into the basement?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Approximately how large was this basement?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Well, it was about 3 by 2, two and a half, the length and the width of the cellar.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What was the floor of the cellar made of?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Earthen.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How was the cellar lit up? How could you see when you were there?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: There was a window which was to the right and there was a door, one entered through a door.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did the window and the door allow light to come into the cellar?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you got into the basement what did you see?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: There was a mattress.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What else did you see?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: A mattress and there was some wood there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see the girl there?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, there was a girl.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you describe the clothes that she had on at that time when you saw her?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I can describe it but I do not remember very, very well, I am sorry. I know that she was dark, that she had black short hair, and it was combed, parted in the middle. She was about 165, 170 metres tall. She was about 17 or 18 of age.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What was this girl doing when you entered the room?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Standing and Zoran Karajica and Cavic were holding her.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What happened next with the girl?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: After a while they began undressing her. They undressed her and shoved her down to the mattress and, as far as I can remember, she had a red bra of a bathing suit and white panties.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When they pushed her down on to the mattress, did someone hold her down?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: She was pushed down on to the mattress and Zoran Karajica and Cavic helped her. After some time Bosko Dragicevic told me to start undressing, and that is to commit the rape of that girl. I was otherwise standing. I looked at Dusko Tadic, what he would tell me, but he did not tell me anything. So I took off my trousers only, and then Dragicevic pushed me on to the girl. I fell across the girl and then after some time I came off on her body, not in.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you ejaculate outside of her body?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When the girl was being held down, was she making any noise or saying anything?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, she was struggling, wrestling, crying, begging not to kill her. She thought, she believed she would be killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was she able to see what was happening or was she blindfolded?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: She was blindfolded. Her eyes were tied.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did she at any stage make an attempt to break away?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, she was struggling and she was trying everything, but she could not because they held on to her arms and her legs.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you ejaculated on the outside of her body what did the other men do?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: They were holding her and Dusko Tadic was standing aside. They were laughing.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What was the next thing that happened after that?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: After that I stood up from the girl and I dressed. After me then Zoran Karajica took his clothes off and lied down on the girl and then he began to commit rape.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did the girl make a noise when Karajica did this?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: She was wrestling and crying, and I could see that that girl was a virgin and that he penetrated her.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How was it that you were able to see she was a virgin?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Well, there was blood her thighs and in between the legs. I am sorry, I do apologise, there was blood there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: After Karajica had raped the girl, did he say something to you?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: They told me that they would bring another girl and that I would have to ejaculate in her, not over her body.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Who said this to you?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: They would bring another girl?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Dragicevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was this the first time that you had ever had sexual relations with a girl?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you remember whether Dusko Tadic said anything to the girl at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Can you hear?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Could you hear the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you remember whether Dusko Tadic said anything to the girl at the time?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: He threatened her, that he would kill her, that he would slit her throat if anybody in the camp ever learned if she, that is, said to anyone what had happened to her.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did the girl say anything to Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did Dusko Tadic say anything to her other than that he would kill her if anyone learned what had happened to her?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Did he say that previously?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No. Did he say anything else to the girl that you can remember? You may not remember.

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When Dragicevic told you that they would choose another girl and that on this occasion you must ejaculate inside her, who was present during this conversation, can you remember? Who of the guards was present?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Nobody was present. Only the two of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: After this incident where did you go?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I went back to my sentry post.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Several hours later on the same day did you see another girl being led out?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Who was leading the girl out on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: There was also Zoran Karajica, Cavic and Dragicevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where did they take the girl?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: To that white house. To the cellar again.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Dragicevic called me, bid me to come with him, and I came with him. Then he threatened me that I had to come on to that girl and Dusko Tadic was there too.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: We went to the cellar of the house where Karajica, Zoran Karajica, Cavic, Dusko Tadic were also there and where Dragicevic arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you recall how Dusko Tadic was dressed on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: He had a camouflage uniform on, a multi-coloured uniform, and he had a pistol on him and a baton and a belt. Bosko Dragicevic was also in uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The camouflage uniform that he had on, what was the main colour of the camouflage uniform?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Multi-coloured police.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What was the main colour, can you remember?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Blue and white. Blue and white, multi-coloured blue and white.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where did you go with this girl and the other men?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: We went to the cellar.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you got to the basement what did you see?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: We saw the girl, Zoran Karajica and Cavic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see Tadic at this stage?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Tadic was there too.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you recall whether the girl was still dressed when you went into the basement?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: About how old was this girl, do you know?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: She was around 17 or 18, something around. She was about 160, 165 tall.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know what her nationality or religion was?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Muslim, that was her nationality.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was she able to see or was she blindfolded?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: She was blindfolded.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you remember and can you describe the clothes that she had on?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: She was wearing a sports suit, that is a sports jacket and trousers. It had red stripes on the side. She had slightly longer hair. She had a pony tail.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you remember what colour her hair was?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Black.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were you told to do something with this girl that was standing there?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, to take her jacket off, to strip her naked, but I took off her jacket and I could not take off anything else because she was wrestling, she was struggling. Zoran Karajica and Cavic undressed her, took her clothes off.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did they strip her naked?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: After they stripped her naked, what did they then do with the girl?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Pushed her down on to the mattress.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When she was pushed on to the mattress, was anyone holding her?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, they held her.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How did they hold her, can you describe that?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Well, they held her hands above her head and they held her feet, her legs.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you remember who it was that was holding her?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: No, I cannot quite remember, but those who were there, I cannot remember who that was specifically, who held on to her arms and who held her legs, but -- I am sorry, I cannot remember who was, who was holding her legs and who was holding her arms, but Milan Cavic and Zoran Karajica held her because they were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When the girl was being held in this position were you told to do something?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, they told me to undress and to lie down on the girl and to perform rape.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What did you do?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I undressed. I lay down on the girl and after some time, I am sorry, as I entered the girl I realised she was a virgin, but Dragicevic pressed me with his foot on my back so that I penetrated the girl. Then after that penetration Dusko Tadic told Dragicevic not to let me off the girl until I came off, until I ejaculated.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you penetrated the girl did she make a sound or make any noise?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you make this girl bleed?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: After you had finished raping the girl, did Tadic say anything to you?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: He told me that I would do what I was told to.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were you upset and confused when this happened?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you attempt to leave the basement ahead of ----

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were you attempting to leave the basement ahead of the other men?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: After I performed the rape?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes, I performed the rape and then I started, I dressed and then I started from the cellar to go back to my guard post and Dusko Tadic caught me by the arm and told me I could not go back to my guard post until we all left.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What happened next?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: After me Cavic took off his clothes and he lay down on the girl and he performed the rape of the girl.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: After Cavic had raped the girl, what did they do with her?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: With the girl?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, what happened next? What was the next thing?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: After Cavic raped her?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, after Cavic had finished raping the girl, what was the next thing that happened?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Then they lifted her off the mattress and removed the blindfold. Then she wiped herself and was ordered to dress. She was also threatened that she would be killed or her throat would be slit, that she was not to talk in the camp about what had happened to her.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Who told her this, that her throat would be slit if she said what had happened to her?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you then all go back to the camp?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: I went to the office until Bosko Dragicevic returned my rifle from the headquarters, because he had left my rifle in the command in the headquarters, and I took my rifle and I went to my sentry post.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see where the other men went?

utterances.speaker: A9
utterances.text: They took the girl to the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am about to move on to another incident. Would that be a convenient time?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will stand in recess until tomorrow at 10 a.m. (5.30 p.m.). (The court adjourned until the following day).
